questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that an interesting project was available. Further, it was a factor that it was a country that I found interesting to get a better understanding of, and that it was a city embrasing student life.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult to find housing in Bologna. Many of the acknowledged housing companies rejected me because I was a student and a foreigner. Further there is a lot of scammers, and I was also a victim. I lost a lot of money and had a period where I did not have any where to live.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware that there is a lot of scam.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were almost nothing availble to students. Whatever were availble either rejected students or required a living period of at least 4 years, which was not a possiblity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was not very good at joining all the trips, parties or sport events that were available, so I do not have an experience of the events. But I am sure it would have been fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I was on many trips, that I am very happy that I experienced. 
Cinque Terre, Toscana, Rimini, Verona. I often took the flixbus, because there was many cheap depatures and the time frame were almost the same as the train.
Bologna was also a very interesting city. I found the museum of Bolognas history very interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
In general it was very easy. I had some very nice coworkers. 
However, it was sometimes a struggle speaking english with some italians in that they refused. Which kind of ruined some good times, in that it made me feel very excluded. This problem was not only experienced at the laboratory, but also a other social places. 

Further the herachial division there is in the italian culture, it quite different from that in Denmark, and I had to get a bit used to that. But my general experience was that they understood my culture as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn a bit Italian, so you can understand a bit, when they stop speaking to you and switch to italian.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely the language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The italian/Bolognese food culture was amazing. Further I had a lot of fun learning the gestures italians make while speaking.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Ask for help to find housing and start early. Learn a bit of italian and enjoy the food culture. For me it was important to make clear for my supervisor that I was there to learn and that i wanted to be part of experiments, before I got some responsibility in the lab.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking a trip to Bologna prior your stay to see the city and meet the people you are about to work with, and maybe try to find a place to live.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the whole experience were good. Trying to live in another country, the project was interesting, the people were nice, the food was amazing, and the trips were very great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Finding a place to live, and coping with the italians not always remembering that you dont understand their language. 
Some pratical stuff regarding the communication with the danish supervisor was also quite challenging at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
